subject: Performance SLO follow-up - Acme AI (cost/perf levers)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@acme.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO follow-up - Acme AI (recap + next steps)

Hi Samir,

Great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery focused on performance and SLOs, plus proposed next steps so we can size the config and cost model for Acme AI. Please confirm any corrections.

Recap (requirements)
- Endpoint: summarization API (sync) and chat stream for end-user UI
- Latency: target p95 ~120ms for summarization; streaming chat should start sending tokens within 150ms of request start
- Throughput: steady 200 rps, expected average token length ~60 tokens per request, occasional spikes to 500 rps for short windows during peak hours
- Concurrency: typical concurrent request count 300, peaks up to 600 for 1-2 minute bursts
- Quality: summary accuracy must be preserved; we are open to quantization if quality regression is within 2% of current baseline

Initial asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm the above numbers and share realistic 15m and 1h peak rates and token distribution samples (sample payloads are helpful)
2) Would you be open to a tech deep-dive with our infra lead (Dev Patel) next week to validate GPU sizing and batching strategy
3) Any regulatory or network constraints we should know about (VPC, private deployment needs)

Cost/performance levers we discussed (high level)
- Continuous batching with small batch latency cap to preserve p95
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated context (saves token compute on common prompts)
- Quantization profiles (int8 or 4-bit) to reduce GPU memory and cost; requires quality validation
- Model variants: use smaller/quantized variants for background workloads and higher-capacity variants for critical paths
- Smart routing: route non-critical requests to cheaper region or cheaper instance types during peak

Ive attached our SLO runbook and a starter cost model to iterate on once you confirm the numbers.

If that looks good I will schedule a 30 minute technical sync including Dev and Rishi. Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: slo-runbook.pdf, cost-model.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up - Acme AI (recommended levers + proposed tech sync)

Appreciate the details Samir. Based on what you shared here are our pragmatic recommendations to meet the p95 and throughput targets while keeping unit cost in check. High level first, then concrete asks for the deep-dive.

Recommended cost/perf levers (practical)
- Continuous batching: target max batching latency cap 8-12ms, progressive batch sizing up to 128 tokens or N requests whichever earlier. This preserves p95 while improving GPU utilization.
- KV/prefix cache: deploy a small in-memory KV cache for repeated prompts and structure prompts so caching hits are more frequent. Expect 20-40% token compute reduction on repetitive traffic.
- Quantization profile: try int8 for first pass; if quality looks good move to 4-bit selectively for non-critical paths. We'll run A/B evals on your test set.
- Model variants and routing: route non-critical async summarization to redwood-medium-quantized, keep redwood-large-int8 for critical interactive sessions. Canary rollout between variants for 5% of traffic to validate quality.
- Autoscaling policy tweaks: warm standby and fast scale-up for 5 minute burst windows to avoid cold-start latency spikes.

Technical sync ask list
- Sample payloads you sent are great. For the sync please have:
  - 15 minute capture of peak traffic (so we can simulate batching behavior)
  - example long requests (~800 tokens) and any multi-turn chat context
  - your preferred SLA window and rollback criteria for canary

I will schedule a 30 minute slot for Thurs 11:00-11:30 PT and include Dev and Rishi. We will bring a short SLO test plan and a preliminary cost model.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: slo-runbook.pdf

Thanks for looping me in. A few infra notes ahead of the sync so we can make the deep-dive more productive.

Preliminary infra sizing and config suggestions
- GPU topology: for steady 250 rps with 60 tokens average, we estimate 2 x A100-40GB or 4 x A10s for the redwood-large-int8 configuration. If you want to aim lower cost, redwood-medium-4bit can run on 2 x A10s but we need to validate quality.
- Batching config: continuous batching with concurrency target 8 per GPU; max batch size 128 tokens and also cap total seq tokens per batch to avoid OOM from long requests
- KV cache: recommend a 2-4 GB per-node in-memory prefix cache for common prompts, eviction LRU and 60s TTL for most conversational flows. See attached diagram for cache placement.
- Quantization profiles: start with int8 kernels for general use, run a controlled 4-bit test on 5% traffic for non-critical microservices. We have pre-built quant profiles; will share during the call.
- Canary rollout: start canary at 2% then 10% then 50% with automated quality checks (token-level BLEU/ROUGE + business metrics).

Ill bring a short script to simulate your peak 15m capture so we can validate p95 live. Attaching KV cache diagram and cost model snapshot.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Infra Lead | Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.com
